title: Xiaomi's open model just exposed the closed AI frontier - TCR 09/22/26
description:
Xiaomi open-sourced MiMo-V2.6-Pro, a 1.02-trillion-parameter model it says matches Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on agent tasks, and live-streamed its reinforcement-learning run; the US and China discussed a possible AI dialogue and incident-notification mechanism as OpenAI called for a US-led global standards coalition; and a zero-day handed any local app full control of Meta's Muse assistant days after launch.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-september-22-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:44 Xiaomi open-sources a trillion-parameter model
3:38 US and China discuss possible AI-incident dialogue
6:41 Meta Muse zero-day and Amazon's block
9:25 British Columbia sues OpenAI over Tumbler Ridge
12:01 Hepatitis B silenced without cutting DNA
15:04 Close

This episode covers Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6-Pro open-weight release and its public training dashboard, the US-China AI-incident notification talks, OpenAI's call for a US-led standards coalition, the Meta Muse zero-day and Amazon's block, British Columbia's lawsuit against OpenAI over the Tumbler Ridge school shooting, California's data-center laws, and a hepatitis B gene-silencing therapy from nChroma Bio.

On September 22, Xiaomi put a trillion-parameter frontier model on the open internet and let anyone watch it being built. MiMo-V2.6-Pro runs 1.02 trillion parameters, 42 billion active per token, ships under an MIT license, and lands within one to four points of Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on several agent benchmarks that measure whether a model can operate software - scoring 46.32 on the Artificial Analysis index, its highest ever open-weight mark. Xiaomi streamed the reinforcement-learning phase on a public dashboard, roughly 750,000 training trajectories in total across two models and 30 steps each in under six days, with the memory crashes and restarts left in the record. As Washington and Beijing discussed a possible AI dialogue and notification mechanism for incidents that threaten national security and OpenAI asked the US to lead a global standards coalition, a phone maker answered the disclosure question from the other end by giving the build process away. A security researcher found a zero-day that hands any local app full control of Meta's Muse assistant, and Amazon blocked Muse for browsing its store without identifying itself. British Columbia sued OpenAI over the Tumbler Ridge school shooting its safety team had flagged and never reported to police. California signed the nation's broadest data-center laws, and researchers silenced hepatitis B in primates by tagging the virus's DNA instead of cutting it.
